description: tcc-prep file ops: access(), ftruncate(), mkstemp(). userspace/ctests/musl_fileops.c. access() is a Stat-based existence check (no perms model). ftruncate() shrinks then grows an open file (kernel Truncate=84 -> VFS ftruncate -> memfs/dunitfs resize), verifying size via fstat and zero-fill on growth. mkstemp() creates a unique temp atomically via O_EXCL. Run: tools/qemu_test.py --build --markers-file tools/m6_fileops_markers.json --post-boot-delay 3 --settle 4 --cmd-timeout 45 --timeout 240 --boot-timeout 120

required.claim: access() reports an existing path present and a missing path absent
ftruncate shrank then grew an open file; fstat saw the new sizes and growth zero-filled
mkstemp created a unique temp file via O_EXCL and filled the template

forbidden.why: access() gave the wrong presence answer
ftruncate or the resulting size/zero-fill was wrong
mkstemp did not create a unique temp file
